title: Mask a bar so only its coating band is exposed
instruction: Mask the bar for coating: lay one masking plate flat on each grey zone so both grey zones are covered and the orange band stays fully uncovered.
context: Masking before spray painting, powder coating or thermal spray is a large share of manual finishing work. A mask has two jobs at once: cover every area that must stay bare, yet leave the whole coating area open, so a plate too far in blocks the band and one too far out leaves bare steel exposed.
setup: A wooden table; all positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, measured forward and toward the left arm. A steel flat bar (140 x 40 x 15 mm, long side running side to side) is held flat in a bench vise, centered 330 mm forward on the midline: two fixed dark-grey steel jaws (140 x 10 x 12 mm) press its front and back faces, their tops 3 mm below the bar's top face so they do not touch the masking area. The bar's top face has a 50 mm wide orange coating band across the middle, with 45 mm of grey bare steel on each side. Two aluminium masking plates (50 mm front to back x 55 mm side to side x 12 mm, 90 g) lie flat on the table 220 mm forward, one 150 mm toward each arm.
scoring: Per side, coverage is measured on a 0.5 mm grid over the bar's top face. Bare steel left exposed on that grey zone counts only plates lying flat on the bar (within 3 mm of resting height, tilted under 5 degrees) and uses each plate's exact outline including its yaw; band covered on that half of the band counts any plate's exact top-down outline at any height or tilt. Both are expressed as the width of an equal-area strip along the 40 mm edge. 0.5 if at most 2 mm of bare steel is exposed and at most 2 mm of the band is covered (a common job-shop masking placement tolerance, +/-0.080 in, about 2 mm); 0.25 if both are within 5 mm; otherwise 0. The score is the sum (1.0 at most). Success once both sides score 0.5 and the plates are still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Lift the plates off and return them to their start positions (tape marks); the bar stays clamped.
fidelity: Rigid boxes; the bar and vise jaws are fixed, the band and grey zones are flush parts of one top face. No paint is sprayed: masking is scored from the plates' exact top-down outlines on a 0.5 mm grid, to a 2 mm per-edge tolerance (a standard masking placement tolerance). Plates are 12 mm thick, not sheet metal, so the gripper can hold them.
